published_statement: RPP 2026, H MASS: '125.13 +- 0.11 OUR AVERAGE. Error includes scale factor of 1.5.' Inputs averaged: 125.04 +- 0.12 (HAYRAPETYAN 25L, CMS 13 TeV ZZ*->4l), 125.10 +- 0.11 (AAD 23BP, ATLAS 13 TeV gg+4l), 125.78 +- 0.26 (SIRUNYAN 20L, CMS 13 TeV gg), 125.09 +- 0.21 +- 0.11 (AAD 15B, LHC Run 1); ideogram chi2 = 6.9, CL = 0.075 (SIRUNYAN 20L contributes 6.2). H DECAY WIDTH: '3.0 +1.5 -0.7 MeV OUR AVERAGE' from AAD 25AQ (ATLAS ZZ, 4.3 +2.7 -1.9), AAD 25AV (ATLAS WW, 0.9 +3.4 -0.9), HAYRAPETYAN 25L (CMS ZZ, 3.0 +2.0 -1.5).
published_hypotheses: m_H: a weighted average of four measurements with total errors, scaled by S = sqrt(chi2/(N-1)) = 1.5 because the inputs are mutually inconsistent at CL 0.075 (PDG listing p.3 ideogram).

m_H inputs: each experiment's mass is a peak-position fit in gg / 4l with signal normalisations floated; ATLAS 2308.04775 treats the H->gg signal-continuum interference as a systematic ('no shift of the mass value is applied'; including SM interference would raise the combination by 15 MeV); CMS 2409.13663 assumes 'the natural width of the Higgs boson is much smaller than the instrumental m4l resolution'.

Gamma_H (PDG p.8, verbatim): 'the total Higgs width cannot be measured indirectly without additional assumptions ... Constraints on the total width from the combination of on-peak and off-peak contributions in Higgs decays to ZZ* rely on the assumption of equal on- and off-shell effective couplings.'

Gamma_H (CMS 2409.13663 abstract, verbatim): determined 'assuming that no new virtual particles affect the production, a premise that is tested by adding new heavy particles in the gluon fusion loop model' (with an unconstrained heavy-quark kappa_Q the CMS value becomes 2.7 +2.7 -1.8 MeV, sec. 11.1).
Gamma_H: SM prediction 4.1 MeV (CMS 2409.13663 sec.1; lifetime 1.6e-22 s); direct on-shell limit only < 330 MeV at 95% CL (resolution-limited).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result, evidence both ways. (1) m_h: the PDG 2024/2025 editions (125.20, the tree's withdrawn pin) lacked CMS's 2024 four-lepton measurement (125.04 +- 0.12, arXiv:2409.13663); with it the 2026 average is 125.13. That IS a case of earlier authors lacking data, and the value moved -- by 0.64 of its own error. Having the datum does not change any conclusion the tree draws: every m_h-dependent figure scales by (125.13/125.20)^k with |k| <= 2, i.e. <= 1.1e-3, and the tree's theorems D15/D16/D18/D19 do not contain the numerical value at all. The average still carries S = 1.5 (CL 0.075) from one outlier; dropping it would move m_h a further ~0.5 sigma, again moving no verdict. (2) Gamma_h: here the missing datum is structural, not a later measurement -- the LHC cannot measure the total width without assuming equal on- and off-shell effective couplings (PDG p.8 verbatim); a model-independent width awaits an e+e- Higgs factory. With the assumption relaxed, the upper bound can weaken by up to ~x2 (arXiv:2603.05020). The Gamma value also moved between editions (3.7 -> 3.0 MeV). Consequence: the tree's order-of-magnitude statements ('gone in ~1e-22 s'; the driven ceiling is sub-femtometre and not a standing displacement) survive every band tested; the single printed digits ('5e-16', '2e-22') do not -- they sit inside the datum's own 68% band and would have printed '4e-16' at the edition the tree previously pinned. Not an error in the source and not a refutation of the tree: a precision the tree prints beyond what the datum and its hypothesis support.
grade_evidence: m_h STANDS in full: the RPP 2026 value 125.13 +- 0.11 GeV was READ at source (pdg.lbl.gov listing p.1) and re-derived exactly from its four inputs (mean 125.1309, chi2 6.92, S 1.518, CL 0.075 -- all PDG numbers reproduced); the capture row and its md5 match the installed particle 1.0.1 source file; every tree figure checked (lambda_h, e-fold, shift, rho_EW/D20 m_h^2 scaling) reproduces. The merged entry is NARROWED because of Gamma_h: the tree uses it as a plain READ value with no hypothesis (excite.py:374, 60-61, 1660-1665; higgs.py:251, 653-658), while the source states it exists only under equal on- and off-shell effective couplings / no new virtual particles in the production (PDG p.8; CMS 2409.13663 abstract) -- a hypothesis the tree drops. Secondary, recorded not repaired: the capture discards the uncertainties (+-0.11 GeV; +1.5/-0.7 MeV) and the S = 1.5 tension; the one-significant-figure Gamma_h outputs ('5e-16' m, '2e-22' s) move within the datum's 68% band (to '4e-16', '3e-22'/'1e-22') and would have printed '4e-16' at the PDG 2024 width -- DATA-DEPENDENT at the printed digit, not at any verdict; and the withdrawn pin 125.20 is under-labelled NAMED-NOT-READ although it is the READable PDG 2024/2025 value. No refusal, theorem or verdict of the tree moves.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names the Gamma_h hypothesis (equal on-/off-shell effective couplings, no new virtual particles in gg -> H*) wherever Gamma_h is used, and carries the published band so the one-figure outputs are printed as a range (ceiling ~3.7e-16..5.2e-16 m; lifetime ~1.5e-22..2.9e-22 s at 68%). To DATA-DEPENDENT at the verdict level: only if some tree conclusion were shown to hinge on the printed digit rather than the order of magnitude -- none found. To WRONG: a measured Gamma_H outside [~0.1, ~100] MeV or an m_H shift of order GeV -- neither is in the literature read here (on-shell limit < 92 MeV, 2609.01385; all m_H inputs within 125.04-125.78). A 2027 RPP average including arXiv:2607.23352 / 2601.05168 / 2609.19948 would re-open the Gamma data row.
